newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh calls for more South Korea investment.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh calls for more South Korea investment.

text.p: Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria urged South Korea on Saturday to invest in Bangladesh, saying his country was striving to end its economic stagnation.
"We have to bring capital from outside to achieve a seven to eight percent economic growth rate," he said while opening the Dhaka branch of South Korea's Hanil Bank.
Kibria said: "Bangladesh, unfortunately, is lagging behind. We cannot match other south Asian nations but insha-allah (god willing) we will come out of economic stagnation."
He said Bangladesh had established a policy giving support to foreign investment. "And that's why the Korean bank is here," he said.
Kibria said Bangladesh had already passed a law allowing foreign countries to set up their own industrial zones in the country to spur economic development and create employment.
He said the country was also stregthening its legal framework to attract investment in the private sector.
South Korea's ambassador in Dhaka, Byun Jong-kyu, said his country would set up an exclusive industrial zone in southern Chittagong.
He expects that some 130 industrial units would be set up in the zone and see more than $1.0 billion in Korean investment coming into Bangladesh in the next 10 years.

"We have been very fortunate to invest in Bangladesh. We have received warm hospitality, found hard-working people and we have political stability here," he told the ceremony marking the bank's opening.
The bank officials said the Hanil Bank would primarily support Korean companies in Banagladesh.
They said there were more than 40 Korean companies in Bangladesh with an investment of over $100 million.
